title: Watering Plants II
interviewTips: State the brute-force approach first before presenting the optimal Two Pointers technique.
Discuss Time and Space complexities upfront before writing code.
Test on empty inputs and single-element edge cases.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Nested Loops (Brute Force)
approaches.intuition: Examine every pair or window using two nested loops, checking conditions repeatedly.
approaches.theory: Checking every subsegment takes quadratic time O(N^2).

approaches.name: Approach 2: Two Pointers / Sliding Window (Optimal)
approaches.intuition: Maintain two pointers (left and right). Expand `right` to include elements and advance `left` when constraints are violated, preserving a valid window state.
approaches.theory: Each pointer moves strictly monotonically from 0 to N. Because each element is processed at most twice (once added, once removed), total operations are strictly 2N = O(N).

timeComplexity.explanation: Each pointer advances at most N times.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Modifies window bounds in place without extra arrays.
